tagline: Up Big Horse Creek to Virginia, crossing it all the way.
intro: NC 194 leaves Warrensville and runs north three and a half miles to Lansing, where Big Horse Creek Road picks up the creek and follows it toward Virginia, crossing it again and again. Now and then the road climbs above the water to look down on narrow valleys of farmhouses, old barns and country churches. At the end of Rip Shin Road the pavement quits for half a mile of Whenlin Ridge Road, and paved Farmers Store Road runs on to the state line.
Ashe County was once one of the state's lost provinces, cut off by the Eastern Continental Divide, where it was said the only way to get there was to be born there.

moments.title: Lansing
moments.text: A town of one stop sign that prospered with the slow Creeper railroad, which served the iron mines and timber trade until the line closed in 1977.

moments.title: Pond Mountain
moments.text: Just west of the road Pond Mountain rises to about 5,000 feet, named by Thomas Jefferson's father for the natural ponds that were scattered over it.

moments.title: Wilburn Waters' grave
moments.text: Wilburn Waters, a hunter and preacher who lived near Tuckerdale, has a gravestone with a bear on top, and a marker in the creek bed below says he killed 120 bears.

practical: About half a mile of Whenlin Ridge Road is gravel.
